current.text: He is a projected starter at forward next to Jalen Suggs, Desmond Bane, Franz Wagner and Wendell Carter Jr.
Orlando has a new head coach, Sean Sweeney, who replaces Jamahl Mosley.
Last season his usage rate was 27, down from 34. He took fewer shots and fewer mid-range jumpers, and his assist rate and share of assisted makes were career highs.
It is unclear whether Sweeney keeps his usage near 27 or pushes it back toward 30. Lloyd hopes the new coach uses him more creatively.
Last season he finished about 125th in nine-cat rankings and 58th in head-to-head rankings.
In category leagues he is fine at picks 50 to 65. Do not take him in the top 50.
An ADP around 32 to 38 is too high for category leagues.
ESPN's category rank of about 75 is too low. Experts would take him before pick 75.
He is the expert's best fantasy target on Orlando. In some category leagues he falls into the 60s and 70s.
In an expert auction mock draft he went for 19 USD. The buyer wanted him for under 20 USD.
His FG% could rise to 47 or 48% if his 3-point percentage improves.
His rim finishing last season was only around the 50th percentile.
Orlando plays 3, 4 and 4 games in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21 (11 games), with 14 back-to-backs this season. Experts call the schedule unremarkable.
Orlando is projected for 47 or 48 wins and the 6th seed.

durable.text: His value comes from volume: strong points, rebounds and assists for a forward.
Turnovers are his worst category. At about 3.1 per game he is a league outlier on the weak side.
His FT% sits around 75% on about 8 attempts per game, which is weak for a forward.
Experts see his FG% and FT% as middling, not damaging. Josh says his free throw shooting has improved to a pretty good level.
He is weak in steals and about average in blocks.
Taking fewer threes is probably better for his fantasy value.
He is worth much more in points leagues than in 9-cat leagues, so points rankings and ADP overrate him for us. Category experts still say he gets too much hate.
He has dealt with a groin strain and still played 72 games last season.
He is probably good for about 70 games.

note: For our 9-cat H2H league, experts value him around picks 50 to 65. That fits his Yahoo rank of 51 and value of 20 USD, and an expert mock auction sold him for 19 USD. Our league's 26 USD last season and his ADP in the 30s come from his much higher points-league appeal. He fits punt TO and punt FT builds best, because his 3.1 turnovers and 75% FT drag those categories while his points, rebounds and assists carry value. Early in the season, check whether new coach Sean Sweeney raises his usage above last season's 27 and whether his FG% moves toward 47%.
